ITEM.PTXT: Electric ACIS (Acoustic Control Induction System) has been adopted and integrated into the resin surge tank by laser welding, reducing the number of parts and weight.

The engine control computer electrically opens and closes the ACIS valve in accordance with the engine speed, throttle valve opening and the cycle of the pulsating flow that changes with engine speed, switching the intake pipe length to increase engine torque.

Pressure fluctuations occur in the intake pipe due to the intermittent intake strokes. The effect that pressure fluctuations remaining in the intake pipe after the intake valve closes have on the next intake stroke is called the pulsation effect. When the pressure fluctuation remaining after the intake valve closes is synchronized with the next intake stroke, the pressure at valve opening becomes higher, so the intake air volume increases and torque can be increased.

To actively utilize this pulsation effect, the variable intake system switches the effective intake pipe length in 2 stages in accordance with the cycle of the pulsating flow that changes with engine speed, increasing torque across the entire range.

Due to the characteristics of the hot-wire type air flow meter, the mass flow rate can in principle be measured directly, so density correction for changes in intake air temperature is not necessary; however, intake air temperature information is required for engine controls such as EFI. Therefore, a compact thermistor type intake air temperature sensor is built into the air flow meter to detect the intake air temperature.

This supplied power is converted into a voltage and output to the engine control computer. MECA.TITLE: MRE Type Cam Position Sensor Operation

ITEM.PTXT: The MRE type cam position sensor consists of a magnet and a sensor circuit (IC) with a built-in MRE.

In the MRE type cam position sensor, the rotation of the timing rotor changes the magnetic vector (direction of the magnetic field) applied to the MRE in the cam position sensor, which changes the internal resistance of the MRE. This resistance change is converted to voltage, and the output waveform is compared with a threshold value and shaped into a rectangular wave of Hi (approximately 4V) and Lo (approximately 1V), which is output to the engine control computer. This output signal is compared with the Ne signal to detect the actual camshaft angle and identify cylinders.

By identifying the position of the timing rotor from the voltage output as Hi/Lo digital signals from when the engine is stopped and from pattern recognition of the peak and valley widths of the timing rotor, the crank position at starting can be detected earlier than with the conventional pickup coil type cam position sensor, improving engine startability.
A highly accurate electromagnetic pickup type sensor has been adopted. Detects the crank position and crank angular velocity.

The timing rotor on the crankshaft has 34 signal teeth with 2 teeth missing for top dead center detection. The crank position sensor detects the crank rotation signal every 10° and can accurately detect top dead center from the missing teeth area.

As the crankshaft rotates, the air gap between the timing rotor protrusions and the crank position sensor changes, so the magnetic flux passing through the coil of the crank position sensor increases and decreases, generating an electromotive force in the coil. Because this generated voltage is reversed when the timing rotor protrusion approaches and moves away from the cam position sensor, it appears as an AC voltage.

A non-contact type accelerator position sensor has been adopted, using a Hall element that can extract the magnetic field strength as an electrical signal using the Hall effect, which provides an output voltage linear to the accelerator pedal depression amount. When the accelerator pedal depression amount changes, the angle of the magnetic field relative to the flow of the applied current in the Hall element changes, so the strength of the magnetic field perpendicular to the applied current changes. The resulting change in voltage, generated perpendicular to both the applied current and the magnetic field, is sent to the engine control computer as the accelerator pedal depression amount signal. In addition, reliability is ensured by adopting a 2-system (main and sub) sensor with different output characteristics.

Engine output is adjusted according to the accelerator opening through fuel injection cut and ignition retard, enabling the vehicle to be driven.
Detects the engine coolant temperature and sends a signal to the engine control computer.

The sensor (zirconia element) is heated by the built-in heater to keep the zirconia element temperature constant and promote feedback control.

The sensor is mounted on the exhaust manifold upstream of the three-way catalyst.
A flat knock sensor has been adopted.
Reliability is ensured by providing 1 sensors each on the left and right inside the V-bank.

When the knock sensor receives vibration from the cylinder block, the movement of the weight lags due to inertia. As a result, pressure is applied to the piezoelectric ceramic provided between the cylinder block and the weight, generating voltage. The voltage is output almost constantly across all frequency bands, and the engine control computer detects the target frequency and determines that knocking is occurring.

The position of the spool valve is controlled by the duty signal from the engine control computer so that the valve timing is always optimum. When the engine is stopped, the spool valve is held by spring force in the most retarded position on the intake side and in the most advanced position on the exhaust side, in preparation for the next start.

When the spool valve of the OCV moves to the position shown in the illustration according to the signal from the engine control computer, hydraulic pressure is applied to the advance side and the camshaft rotates toward the advance side.

When the spool valve of the OCV moves to the position shown in the illustration according to the signal from the engine control computer, hydraulic pressure is applied to the retard side hydraulic chamber and the camshaft rotates toward the retard side.

The engine control computer calculates the target advance angle according to the driving conditions and performs control. After the target timing is set, the timing is held by keeping the OCV in the neutral position unless the driving conditions change. This adjusts the valve timing to any target position while preventing unnecessary outflow of engine oil.

A 12-hole ultra-fine atomization fuel injector has been adopted. The injector is mounted directly on the cylinder head, and the tip of the fuel injector protrudes into the intake port, shortening the distance to the combustion chamber. This reduces fuel adhesion to the intake port, achieving low fuel consumption and low emissions.
A circumferential flow type in-tank fuel pump has been adopted.
By integrating the charcoal canister, fuel filter, pressure regulator and fuel sender gauge into the fuel pump assembly, weight has been reduced and space in the engine room has been saved.
By placing a coil independently for each cylinder, the distributor and high-tension cords are eliminated, reducing losses in the high-voltage section, ensuring reliability and reducing radio noise.
A compact, lightweight igniter is built in, and a high voltage is induced in the secondary (No. 2) coil by the signal from the engine control computer.
The canister purge volume is controlled by the signal (duty signal) from the engine control computer. The purge volume is determined by the ratio of the ON and OFF times of the signal (duty ratio).
The EFI-L method, which detects the intake air volume with the air flow meter and controls the fuel injection volume, has been adopted.
Independent injection (each cylinder injected 1 time(s) per 2 crankshaft revolutions) has been adopted as the injection method.

Fuel injection consists of synchronous injection, in which the basic injection duration is corrected with signals from each sensor and fuel is always injected at the same position, and asynchronous injection, in which fuel is injected when an injection request is detected from the signals of each sensor regardless of crank angle. Also, to protect the engine and improve fuel economy, fuel cut is performed to temporarily stop fuel injection according to driving conditions.

Corrects for the operation delay of the injectors.

The driver's operation (accelerator pedal depression amount) is transmitted to the engine control computer by the accelerator position sensor located on the accelerator pedal. The engine control computer determines the throttle opening appropriate to the driving conditions and drives the electronic throttle motor. The throttle valve opening is fed back to the engine control computer by the throttle position sensor.

A DC motor with good response and low power consumption is used for the throttle valve drive motor, and a non-contact type throttle sensor has been adopted, achieving a lightweight and compact construction.
The insides of both the accelerator position sensor and the throttle position sensor have a 2-system (main and sub) configuration, and the system is constantly monitored for malfunctions.

If a malfunction is detected, the warning light in the meter alerts the driver and current to the motor is cut. The throttle valve is returned to a predetermined opening by the throttle valve return spring. Engine output is adjusted according to the accelerator opening through fuel injection cut and ignition retard, enabling the vehicle to be driven.
A 1-shaft type electronic accelerator pedal with a built-in accelerator position sensor has been adopted, reducing size and weight.
Reliability is ensured by adopting a 2-system (main and sub) sensor with different output characteristics.

The position of the spool valve is controlled by the duty signal from the engine control computer so that the valve timing is always optimum. ITEM.PTXT: The SRS airbags, driver SRS knee airbag and seat belts with pretensioners are ignited by the impact of a frontal collision. The determination is made based on the front airbag sensor signals and the signals from the G sensor and electronic safing sensor in the center airbag sensor (computer).
The SRS side airbag is ignited when both the side airbag sensor signal from a side impact and the electronic safing sensor in the center airbag sensor (computer) turn ON.

The SRS curtain shield airbag is ignited by the ignition signal of the SRS side airbag that satisfies the above conditions, or when both the rear side airbag sensor signal and the electronic safing sensor in the center airbag sensor (computer) turn ON.
To keep a record of deployment, the center airbag sensor (computer) keeps the SRS airbag warning light illuminated even after the primary check. This SRS airbag warning light cannot be cleared.
The operation of the diagnosis circuit is indicated by the SRS airbag warning light in the meter. The diagnosis circuit operates in 2 periods: the primary check and the constant check.

When the engine switch is turned to IG ON, the SRS airbag warning light illuminates for approximately 6 seconds and the primary check is performed. During this period, ignition is prohibited and the operation of the center airbag sensor is diagnosed. If a malfunction is detected during this primary check, the SRS airbag warning light remains illuminated and does not go off even after 6 seconds have elapsed.
For a center airbag sensor that has deployed the airbags, the SRS airbag warning light remains illuminated even after the primary check, regardless of whether there is a malfunction.

After the primary check is completed and the SRS airbag warning light goes off, the system enters the ignition-enabled state, and the diagnosis circuit constantly checks the system for malfunctions. If a malfunction is detected during this constant check, the SRS airbag warning light illuminates. (The warning indication for low power supply voltage goes off after the power supply voltage returns to normal.)

By switching to the diagnosis mode, the diagnosis result for the malfunction location can be displayed by the number of times the indicator light blinks. In addition, a new diagnosis function has been adopted, and the diagnostic trouble code for the malfunction location can be read by connecting a diagnostic tool to DLC3. For details on the diagnosis mode, refer to the Repair Manual.

When the start signal (STSW) from the engine switch is input, the engine control computer sends a signal (STAR) to the starter relay through the neutral start switch to operate the starter. At this time, the engine control computer turns ON the ACC cut (ACCR) to prevent flickering of the meter, clock, audio, etc.

After the starter starts operating, the engine control computer continues to output a signal to the starter until it detects that the engine has started running. After cranking, when the computer determines that the engine has started, it stops outputting the signal to the starter relay.

By lowering the generated voltage when the vehicle is idling or driving at constant speed and raising it during deceleration, the engine load due to alternator power generation is reduced, lowering engine fuel consumption. In addition, during acceleration, the generated voltage is adjusted so that the integrated current value approaches the target value.
The integrated current value is the integrated value of the battery input/output current detected by the current sensor.

Installed on the negative terminal of the battery, it detects the battery charge/discharge current and sends a signal to the engine control computer. Based on this signal, the engine control computer calculates the battery capacity. A Hall IC is used to detect the charge/discharge current; it converts the change in magnetic flux density generated in the core by the battery charge/discharge current into a voltage and outputs it.

If the battery fluid temperature is too low or too high, it can accelerate battery deterioration or cause the battery to discharge. Also, since the current acceptance characteristics change with battery fluid temperature, the battery is protected by detecting the battery fluid temperature and sending a signal to the engine control computer.
The battery temperature sensor is built into the battery current sensor. As a result, the sensor is located near the negative terminal, where it is less affected by engine heat.

When a sensor malfunctions, or when the engine control computer judges it necessary based on battery condition, electrical load operating status, etc., alternator charging control is stopped and the system switches to constant voltage generation mode.
